query: What business models and customers do these companies describe?

per_column.name: business_model_type
per_column.rationale: How a company creates and captures value (SaaS, marketplace, professional services) is a core constitutive aspect OF its business profile.

per_column.name: primary_customer_segment
per_column.rationale: Who the company serves (B2B enterprise, B2C, developers) is an intrinsic aspect OF the business profile and directly targeted by the query.

per_column.name: industry_vertical
per_column.rationale: The sector/domain the company operates in (fintech, healthtech) is a genuine descriptive facet OF the business profile.

per_column.name: core_product_service_category
per_column.rationale: What the company actually sells (software platform, physical device, investment fund) is a constitutive part of the profile, though it overlaps heavily with business_model_type and delivery_mode.

per_column.name: delivery_mode
per_column.rationale: How the offering reaches customers (cloud, in-person, physical retail) is an aspect OF the business profile, but its value space largely re-encodes product category and business model distinctions.

judge.rationale: All five columns are legitimate part-of facets of a company business profile rather than external predictors or causes, so the meronymy requirement is satisfied. However mutual exclusivity is only moderate: business_model_type, core_product_service_category, and delivery_mode substantially overlap. Their value spaces re-encode the same underlying distinction repeatedly -- e.g. SaaS (model) / software_platform (product) / cloud_only (delivery) all describe the same cloud-software company, and staffing_services / staffing_consulting / in_person_services likewise collapse into one aspect. This is largely one 'what/how it's sold' facet split three ways, which lowers mutual exclusivity. Exhaustiveness is strong: model, customer, vertical, and product together cover the main constitutive dimensions the query cares about (business models and customers), with only minor gaps (e.g. company stage/scale or geographic scope).
